result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.add_pa_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a Barabási-Albert preferential attachment graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L3911-L3963){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_pa_graph( n, m=2, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Preferential attachment graph](/assets/graphs/add-pa-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three preferential attachment graphs on eight nodes, placed on a ring in arrival order, for m=1, 2, and 3 edges per new node. The first node, in the accent color, collects the most links in every panel (degree 6, 5, and 7), showing how early, well-connected nodes become hubs." width="100%"} Grows a graph by adding nodes one at a time, with each new node connecting to `m` existing nodes with probability proportional to degree. This creates scale-free networks with power-law degree distributions. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes to add. [m]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[2]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of edges to attach from each new node. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for reproducibility. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Each new node attaches to `m` existing nodes chosen with probability proportional to their current degree, so already well-connected nodes tend to accumulate even more connections. This "rich get richer" dynamic is what produces the scale-free, power-law degree distribution the Barabási-Albert model is known for: ::: {#9e3edca7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_pa_graph(n=100, m=3, seed=23) ) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (100, 294) ``` ::: :::
